excerpt: Page | 4 Introduction: Student life on campus is of paramount importance, as the professional and personal growth of students heavily depends on their experiences on campus. Best Practices and Standard operating procedures evolved over the years and were conceptualized by various personnel handling Student Affairs. They are collated and presented in this manual, which will serve as a guideline for managing student affairs personally. Objective: To create a system for handling all student-related issues with the active support of campus administration and school heads VISION: To aid the organization in providing education for LIFE by imparting eternal values and skills needed to mold a Personality suited for Professional Growth in a Rapidly Evolving World MISSION: To be at the service of students to Enhance their LIFE at Amrita both professionally and personally. Discipline Human behaviour is governed by the mind, brain, and emotions. Without focus and proper training of the mind, achieving success becomes challenging. The process of mental discipline requires consistent and deliberate effort, underscoring its critical importance. Universit y students, being in a transitional phase of adolescence, often possess abundant energy that, if not properly directed, can lead to adverse outcomes for both their personal development and the university community. Therefore, maintaining discipline and addressing acts of indiscipline are vital responsibilities of the Office of Student Affairs. excerpt: Page | 7 Handling of Emergency situation in the campus–Standard Operating Procedure 1. Riot on the Campus Security must be notified immediately. Upon receiving the information, security personnel should promptly inform the Chief Warden and the Professor of Student Welfare (OSA). The Chief Warden, Professor of Student Welfare, and relevant staff from the concerned department residing on campus should arrive at the location as soon as possible (ASAP) to assess the situation. Emergency Response Team formed by the management also will be present at the location. Staff from the concerned department should engage with the students involved to understand the issue and help defuse the situation. If the incident involves serious injury to an individual or significant damage to university property, the Public Relations Officer (PRO) must be informed, and they will coordinate with the police for necessary intervention. 2. Following discussions with the Dean Academics, concerned School heads/Dean and Campus Administration, if deemed necessary: a. Students residing in the hostel may be instructed to vacate. b. Academic sessions may be suspended indefinitely to ensure safety and stability on campus.

excerpt: Page | 16 Events Planning and Execution Guidelines Events promote intellectual, cultural, and personal growth, helping students discover and hone their talents while fostering creativity and leadership. Events create a sense of belonging by bringing students, faculty, and staff together, strengthening bonds within the university community. Celebrations of festivals like Gokulashtami, Onam, and Navratri help preserve traditions and encourage cultural exchange among diverse student populations. Events provide a break from academic rigor, encouraging relaxation and rejuvenation through fun and engaging activities. Any events apart from University accreditation, Department workshops and Anokha all events meant for students at Coimbatore campus are channelized/conducted through OSA.. Events, Proposal, Budgets, and arrangements are verified and forwarded for the ADSA approval through Faculty Student Welfare. Role of the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) The OSA plays a central role in planning, coordinating, and executing events effectively, ensuring they align with the university’s vision and values. Club Formation and Structure: Each club must have a faculty advisor, a student coordinator, and an executive committee. Additional faculty/Staff can be identified as co-advisor based on the strength and number of activity of the club. Clubs must register with the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) at the start of the academic year. Provide a club charter outlining objectives, activities, and the annual plan. Election/Nomination of Student Bearers: Election Process: Clubs may elect student bearers (President, Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer) through democratic elections, ensuring transparency and fairness. Nomination Process: Alternatively, bearers can be nominated by the faculty advisor based on academic performance, leadership skills, and active participation in non-academic activities. Student who are having arrears and discipline actions are not eligible. Activity Proposals Proposals for

Activity Proposals Proposals for activities/events should include objectives, timelines, target audience, and estimated budgets. Dates proposed for the Event by the club should not have a clash with the University/Other major events planned by departments. Submit proposals to OSA for approval at least 3 weeks before the event. Coordinate with other clubs to avoid overlapping schedules. Club should actively respond to invitations from the University to organize events whenever asked for. Club coordinators are encouraged to identify and nominate talented students within their clubs for prestigious events such as AIU and National UNIFEST. Documentation and Reporting Maintain records of all events, including attendance, videos, photos, and feedback. Submit an activity report to OSA within 5 days of event completion.
